title: Bulgarian St. Stephen Church

buildingCutout.basis: The standing cast-iron church’s named native outline.

terrainReference.basis: Unchanged source ground beneath the public entrance steps at the Golden Horn church.

mapIdentity.provider: Named OpenStreetMap cast-iron church and its mapped main entrance.
mapIdentity.scope: The named Istanbul footprint fixes the two long walls and the five-sided apse. The 1895 German trade journal records a 15 m width and a 30 m bell tower to the cross. The present mapped shell is about 15.2 m wide and 27 m long to the apse, so the model uses the actual mapped face locations.

note: The July 1895 Stahl und Eisen photograph and full plate show the built ironwork in the Waagner works yard before shipment. The Orthodox Patriarchate and the municipal restoration team document the standing basilica, five-sided apse and zinc-coated sheet roof.
